description: MacBook Pro 16-inch M2 Max (j416c, t6021), Aurora kernel, converged image-2 install: raw host answers for record mode
source: Real evidence from the M2 Max, 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-26: diagnostics/m2-usbc-20260913 (kernel log, device tree), outputs/m2-image2-acceptance/41-deferred-evidence.txt (offline first-boot failure), operations/asahi-brcmfmac-6ghz-73/logs/boot-1-failure.log (5 GHz first join), operations/logind-usb-connector/issue.md (lid close with a USB-C monitor attached). The inventory answers come from the booted kernel's own package, linux-aurora 7.1.12.aurora2-2 and its headers (device tree, module aliases, build config), and the kernel log's failed AVD probe. The live audio, display and keyboard-light answers come from outputs/m2-image2-acceptance/ (37-audio-state.txt, 37-mic-capture.txt, 37-speakersafetyd-unit.txt, 39-display-check-session.txt, owner-look-listen.sh), with the panel backlight level and the volume reconstructed and noted. The M2 has since been reinstalled with converged image 4, so image 2's own answers (mac-check, encryption, the backlight level, the volume) can no longer be captured and stay reconstructed; tests/corpus/m2-max-converged is its real run. The camera, function-key and ports answers are stand-ins, noted on each entry (checks added after image 2's runs).
pseudonymized: Committed evidence is pseudonymized: every Wi-Fi network name, MAC address, IP address, UUID, boot id and account name in it was swapped for a fake of the same shape, and the camera module's serial (in the ISP's log lines), before commit, so the corpus exercises the scrubber on real log formats without publishing the real values. 'forbidden' lists the identifiers (decoys and lab hostnames) that must never survive into a recording or report.

rate = 48000
n = 2 * rate

argv:
for p in /sys/class/typec/port*; do
  n=${p##*/port}
  case $n in ''|*[!0-9]*) continue;; esac
  if [ -e "/sys/class/typec/port$n-partner" ]; then partner=yes; else partner=no; fi
  data=$(sed -n 's/.*\[\(.*\)\].*/\1/p' "$p/data_role" 2>/dev/null)
  power=$(sed -n 's/.*\[\(.*\)\].*/\1/p' "$p/power_role" 2>/dev/null)
  echo "typec $n partner=$partner data=$data power=$power"
done
for d in /sys/bus/usb/devices/*; do
  [ -r "$d/speed" ] || continue
  case ${d##*/} in *:*) continue;; usb*) kind=root;; *) kind=device;; esac
  class=$(cat "$d/bDeviceClass" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$class" = 00 ]; then class=$(cat "$d"/*:*/bInterfaceClass 2>/dev/null | head -n 1); fi
  echo "usb $kind speed=$(cat "$d/speed") class=$class"
done

argv:
swipe=$(hyprctl getoption gestures:workspace_swipe 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^int: *//p')
[ -n "$swipe" ] && echo "swipe-live $swipe"
field() { printf '%s\n' "$1" | sed -nE "s/.*$2=\"?([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\"?([,;}].*)?$/\1/p"; }
n=0
for f in "$HOME"/.local/share/omarchy/default/hypr/*.lua "$HOME"/.local/share/omarchy/default/hypr/*.conf \
         "$HOME"/.config/hypr/*.lua "$HOME"/.config/hypr/*.conf; do
  [ -r "$f" ] || continue
  n=$((n + 1))
  { sed -e 's/--.*$//' -e 's/#.*$//' "$f" | tr -d ' \t' | tr '\n' ';'; echo; } |
    sed -e 's/^/;/' -e 's/hl\./\nhl./g' -e 's/;gesture=/\ngesture=/g' -e 's/;workspace_swipe=/\nworkspace_swipe=/g' |
    while IFS= read -r c; do
      case $c in
        'hl.gesture({'*)
          c=${c%%\}*}
          [ "$(field "$c" fingers)" = 3 ] || continue
          action=$(printf '%s\n' "$c" | sed -nE 's/.*action="([a-z]+)"([,;].*)?$/\1/p')
          case $action in workspace|unset) ;; *) action=other;; esac
          echo "gesture 3 $(field "$c" direction) $action";;
        'gesture=3,'*)
          c=${c#gesture=}; c=${c%%;*}
          old=$IFS; IFS=,; set -- $c; IFS=$old
          dir=$2; shift 2; action=other
          for a in "$@"; do case $a in *:*) ;; workspace|unset) action=$a; break;; *) break;; esac; done
          echo "gesture 3 $dir $action";;
        'workspace_swipe='*)
          case ${c#workspace_swipe=} in true*|1*|yes*|on*) echo "workspace-swipe 1";; *) echo "workspace-swipe 0";; esac;;
      esac
    done
done
echo "files $n"

/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/94-omarchy-mac-bat.text:
# Reapply the charge limit saved by omarchy-battery-charge-limit when the Apple SMC battery appears.
ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="power_supply", KERNEL=="macsmc-battery", RUN+="/usr/lib/omarchy-mac/battery-charge-limit-restore"

/usr/lib/omarchy-mac/battery-charge-limi.text:
#!/bin/bash
# udev runs this as the SMC battery appears, so a saved charge limit survives
# reboots. It never fails the event: anything unexpected leaves the SMC alone.
set -euo pipefail

saved_file="/etc/udev/macsmc-battery.conf"
end_file="/sys/class/power_supply/macsmc-battery/charge_control_end_threshold"

[[ $(omarchy-hw-platform 2>/dev/null) == "apple-silicon" ]] || exit 0
[[ -r $saved_file && -w $end_file ]] || exit 0

limit=""
while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n $line ]]; do
  if [[ $line == CHARGE_CONTROL_END_THRESHOLD=* ]]; then
    limit=${line#*=}
  fi
done <"$saved_file"

if [[ $limit == "80" || $limit == "100" ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' "$limit" >"$end_file" || true
fi
/usr/lib/omarchy-mac/battery-charge-limi.note: omarchy-mac 62's lib/battery-charge-limit-restore, which the rule runs (62-battery-restore-sim.txt ran it on image 2)
